done.why: I wanted to find treasure and keep it safe. I got four treasures into the trophy case, and the walk up the chimney with one item per trip was getting repetitive. A thief had taken my jade figurine and I didn't know how to go after him, so I stopped while I was ahead.

about: You're at an old white house, and under it is a big underground world full of treasure. Getting treasure is half the job. The other half is getting it back up to the trophy case in the living room. The trap door slams shut and gets barred behind you, so the only way back up is a narrow chimney that fits you, your lamp and one other thing. Meanwhile somebody unseen walks off with anything you leave lying around.

ending.what: I didn't reach an ending. I stopped with 4 treasures in the case (painting, trident, bracelet, platinum bar) and a score of 95 out of 350, ranked Novice Adventurer.

moments.note: It didn't understand 'can I go around the house?', but 'walk around the house' worked.
'open the window wider' got 'You can't see any such thing' even though the window was right there. One extra word broke it.
The trophy case 'has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.' Now I knew where treasure goes.
'go down the trap door' got 'You can't do that!', but plain 'go down' worked.
The trap door crashed shut and someone barred it. I was trapped underground.
I killed the troll with one swing. Easier than it looked.
Touching the mirror made a rumble, but the room looked the same. I couldn't tell if I had moved.
My first treasure, Poseidon's crystal trident, lying on a shore.
A vampire bat grabbed me and dropped me in a coal mine maze where every room is 'nondescript'.
Too heavy to take the bracelet ('the sword not least of it'). I had to go back down and drop stuff.
'take out the garlic' got 'You're not in that!', which made no sense to me.
With the garlic, the bat was 'obviously deranged and holding his nose'. I worked that out myself.
The chimney refusal listed exactly what I carried and said room for 'you, your lamp and one thing more'. Very clear.
The trap door slams and gets barred again every time I go down, so every treasure needs its own chimney trip.
The jade figurine and the manual were gone from the studio where I'd left them. Someone stole them while I was ferrying the others.
The platinum bar just echoed 'Bar bar...'. Shouting 'echo' changed the room and then I could take it.

wished: Ask in plain words which ways I could go from the Round Room
Carry more than one thing up the chimney, or wedge the trap door open so I didn't have to ferry treasures one at a time
Find out who stole my jade figurine and chase them
Phrase things naturally ('go down the trap door', 'take out the garlic', 'drop everything except the lantern') and be understood
Swim across the lake at Reservoir North

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: This gave me my goal without anyone telling me. The case was where my treasure should go.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: This was scary, and it shaped the whole rest of the game.

lines.line: a large vampire bat who is obviously deranged and holding his nose.
lines.why: Funny, and a reward for figuring out what the garlic was for.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A rule told to me plainly. I understood the puzzle right away.

lines.line: Fortunately, there is still one chance for you to be a vandal
lines.why: I liked the wink. The gallery invites you to steal.

fun.why: Putting each treasure in the case felt good, and the garlic and echo tricks were satisfying. The ferrying trips got repetitive.

engagement.why: Being locked in, getting snatched by the bat and then robbed kept me alert and wanting to get my things safe.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were fair, and the chimney rule was explained clearly. My trouble was mostly the parser rejecting natural phrasing, plus the random coal mine.

interestingness.why: Getting the treasure home is the real puzzle: a trap door that bars itself, a chimney that takes one item, and a thief. That made 'keep it safe' mean something.

prose.why: Witty and clear when it describes things. The many one-word room replies like 'Kitchen' felt thin, and the error messages were cryptic.
